fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled MAT file bytes are written to a temp file and opened; the file header is parsed and version is set to MAT_FT_MAT5.
Mat_VarReadNextInfo dispatches to Mat_VarReadNextInfo5 for a v5 file, which parses the compressed variable tag (MAT_T_COMPRESSED) and sets matvar->compression = MAT_COMPRESSION_ZLIB.
The attacker-controlled dimensions (e.g., 1000 x 1000) are decompressed from the zlib stream and stored in matvar->dims; the product nelems = 1000000 is later computed by SafeMulDims.
datapos is set to the file offset where the remaining compressed data payload begins; the z_stream avail_in is zeroed so Mat_VarRead5 can continue inflating from this offset.
Mat_VarReadDataAll calls ReadData which dispatches to Mat_VarRead5 for the MAT_FT_MAT5 file.
nelems is computed as the product of the attacker-controlled dims (1000*1000 = 1000000).
The class type from the array flags is MAT_C_CHAR, entering the character-data branch.
The data tag is inflated from the compressed stream; packed_type is set from the tag and nBytes is taken from the tag (attacker-controlled, e.g., 100).

fine_trace.code: matvar->data_type = packed_type; matvar->data_size = Mat_SizeOf(matvar->data_type); matvar->nbytes = nBytes;
fine_trace.note: matvar->nbytes is set to the attacker-controlled nBytes (100) from the data tag, and data_size is set to Mat_SizeOf(packed_type).
A heap buffer of only nBytes+1 (101) bytes is allocated for the character data.

ReadCompressedCharData calls InflateData with len=nelems (1000000) and data_size=Mat_SizeOf(packed_type), inflating nelems*data_size bytes into the 101-byte buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow write.
